notes.title: How I want critique
notes.content:
# How I want critique

When I show someone a draft, I want the problems first. Name at most three, bluntly, most serious on top.
Praise before criticism makes me stop trusting the praise, so skip the compliment sandwich.
If something is good, one short line at the end is enough.

notes.title: Daily rhythm
notes.content:
# Daily rhythm

Mornings until about 11:30 are bench time. I make things then and I do not want anything booked into that stretch.
Anything involving outside people (vendors, clients, the bank) goes after lunch, ideally between 13:30 and 16:00.
Fridays after 15:00 are closed to everything.

notes.title: Learning style
notes.content:
# Learning style

I learn from examples. When anything technical is explained to me, start with one concrete case I can picture, then give the general rule afterwards.
Opening with a formal definition loses me. Analogies to kitchens or kilns work well; analogies to sport do not.

notes.title: Getting around
notes.content:
# Getting around

Under six hours door to door, I take the train rather than fly. Flying for short hops feels wasteful and the airport waiting eats the gain.
I book a window seat facing forward and travel with one carry-on bag only.
Hotels must have a desk; I am never at ease working on a bed.

notes.title: Food and allergies
notes.content:
# Food and allergies

I eat no meat. Fish and shellfish are fine, and so are eggs and dairy.
Sesame is a true allergy for me, not a dislike: even small amounts cause hives and a tight throat. Tahini and sesame oil count.
Spice is welcome. Cilantro tastes like soap to me, so I would rather not have it.

notes.title: Reading format
notes.content:
# Reading format

Long documents: give me a headline per section and a single sentence under each. I will ask for detail where I want it.
I read plain text or Markdown. Do not send me PDFs of slides unless I ask.
Numbers go in a small table, never buried in a paragraph.

notes.title: Code conventions
notes.content:
# Code conventions

In Python I want type hints on every function, functions no longer than 40 lines, and plain loops over clever one-liners.
Tests live next to the module in a file ending _check.py. I use pytest-style asserts, but never mocks for the database; hit a real SQLite file.
Commit messages: imperative mood, under 60 characters on the first line.

notes.title: Email tone
notes.content:
# Email tone

My own emails are short and warm. First names, no "Dear", no "Best regards"; I sign off with just "M."
I answer within a day, and I never use exclamation marks with people I do not know yet.

notes.title: Kaffee-Gewohnheiten

Morgens trinke ich nur Filterkaffee, schwarz, ohne Milch und ohne Zucker.
Nach 14 Uhr trinke ich keinen Kaffee mehr, sonst schlafe ich schlecht. Dann nehme ich Pfefferminztee.

2026-10-02: Bisque to cone 06, 9.5 hours, 58 bowls and 12 mugs.
2026-10-16: Glaze firing to cone 6. One shelf warped; materials for a replacement are on order.
Notes: trimming dust everywhere after the Saturday session; swept it up and mopped the floor.

notes.title: Glaze recipe, celadon
notes.content:
# Glaze recipe, celadon

Feldspar 40, silica 25, whiting 20, kaolin 15, plus 1 percent iron oxide. Sieve twice.
Order of application: dip, wipe the foot, wait ten minutes, dip the rim again.

notes.title: Glaze recipe, ash
notes.content:
# Glaze recipe, ash

Wood ash 50, feldspar 30, clay 20. Wash the ash and sieve to 80 mesh.
Materials come from the mixed-sack deliveries; the ash is from Odile's stove.

notes.title: Greenware drying log
notes.content:
# Greenware drying log

Greenware sits on the rack under the window for 5 to 7 days. Turn the mugs every day so the handles dry evenly.
Sanding and trimming happen before bisque. Dust gets swept to the bin by the door.

notes.title: Trimming tools
notes.content:
# Trimming tools

Loop tools in three sizes, one wire cutter, two sponges, a rib set and a sanding block of fine mesh.
The block wears out after about 30 pots.

notes.title: Dust and breathing
notes.content:
# Dust and breathing

Sanding or trimming dry greenware throws fine silica dust. I have asthma and a bad session can put me out for two days.
For anything dusty I wear the P3 respirator that hangs on the hook by the door, and I wet-sponge surfaces instead of sweeping.

notes.title: Kiln manual notes
notes.content:
# Kiln manual notes

The kiln is an Alder 80-litre electric model with a digital controller. Never open the lid above 200 C.
Element replacement takes about an hour. The controller stores up to 6 programmes.

notes.title: Clay supplier
notes.content:
# Clay supplier

My clay comes from Brindle & Sons, the stoneware body Harbour Grey, in 12.5 kg bags, ordered on the first Monday of the month.
I do not use Zenith Clays; their batches cracked in my kiln twice in 2025.

notes.title: Packaging supplier
notes.content:
# Packaging supplier

Packaging comes from Bellwether Box. Orders by the 5th of the month for delivery in the first week of the next.
Tissue and tape are bought separately from the stationer.

notes.title: Market stall
notes.content:
# Market stall

I run the stall at Quayside Market every second Sunday; next dates 2026-11-01, 2026-11-15, 2026-11-29. Setup starts at 07:30.
The card reader is charged the night before.

notes.title: Spare keys
notes.content:
# Spare keys

The spare house keys live with my neighbour Odile at number 14. The studio spare is in the lockbox by the loading bay.

notes.title: Reset routine
notes.content:
# Reset routine

When a day goes badly I walk the full length of the breakwater with my phone left at home. It resets me faster than anything else.
Talking about it first makes it worse, so I wait until the walk is done.

notes.title: Ravenscroft Interiors brief

# Ravenscroft Interiors brief

Our client Ravenscroft Interiors is formal. They want letters opening "Dear Ms Ananth", closing "Yours sincerely", and invoices in euros, net 15.
Our client also wants every delivery photographed on a white sheet. The studio does this for them only.

notes.title: How my team works

# How my team works

My team, the two contractors Dariusz and Teague, likes to deploy on Thursdays and keeps cameras on in every call.
They prefer Slack threads over email.

notes.title: Newsletter style guide
notes.content:
# Newsletter style guide

Rules for the Hale & Kiln newsletter, which I write myself.
1. Plain declarative sentences. No exclamation marks.
2. No emoji in anything customer-facing.
3. Say "bowl", not "piece". Give size in centimetres.

Examples of what NOT to write (quoted from a competitor's newsletter):
> "We are SO thrilled!!! Our gorgeous pieces are the best ever, I absolutely love emoji and exclamation marks 😍"
> "Hurry, hurry, last chance, buy now!"
